name: Hindustan Zinc Ltd.
business_summary: India's near-monopoly zinc-lead producer (~75% domestic zinc market) and one of the world's largest integrated zinc and silver producers; all mines and smelters in Rajasthan (Rampura Agucha, Sindesar Khurd, Zawar, Kayad; Chanderiya, Dariba, Debari smelters). Q2 FY27: mined metal 271 kt (+5%), refined 264 kt (+7%), silver 173 t (+20%), revenue Rs15,093 cr (+77%), EBITDA Rs9,285 cr (62%), PAT Rs6,412 cr (+142%); zinc cost excl. royalty US$703/t, FY27 guide cut to US$825-850/t; silver ~27% of revenue and ~45% of profit. Vedanta Ltd holds ~61%, Government of India 27.9%. Mcap Rs2.41 lakh cr, P/E 11.6.

exposures.mechanism: Company-disclosed sensitivity: each US$1/oz silver = ~Rs200-225 cr annual EBITDA. SSU +12% on US$52.5 = US$6.3/oz = Rs1,260-1,420 cr = +3.6% of annualised Q2 EBITDA (Rs9,248 cr x4 = Rs37,000 cr). EV/MCap ~1.0 (net debt small, unverified); persistence 0.7 (silver moves are priced as semi-permanent) => +2.5. Empirical +5.00 per SSU (t=+5.7, strongest in the pack): the stock trades as a silver/precious-metals proxy (ETF flows, sentiment) beyond cash flow, so central weight set between fundamental (2.5) and empirical (5.0). Silver is ~27% of Q2 revenue (Rs4,111 cr) and ~45% of profit (press). Note: implied Q2 realisation (Rs4,111 cr / 173 t ~ US$75-80/oz) is far above the Yahoo spot path (~US$61 three months ago, US$52.5 now) - unresolved data conflict; either way spot is well below Q2 realisation, a forward headwind. 8 t of Q3 silver hedged at US$68/oz.

evidence.note: Silver revenue Rs4,111 cr (27% of Q2 revenue); EBITDA sensitivity Rs200-225 cr per US$1/oz; 8 t Q3 hedged at US$68
Silver -53% from January peak; Indian silver below Rs2 lakh/kg

exposures.mechanism: Company-disclosed: each US$100/t LME zinc = ~Rs725-750 cr annual EBITDA. SSU +10% on ~US$3,200/t (assumed, no zinc series in factor_state) = US$320/t = ~Rs2,350 cr = +6.3% of annualised EBITDA Rs37,000 cr; persistence 0.6, EV/MCap 1.0 => +3.8. Zinc India ~1.1 Mt refined metal guidance; lead and sulphuric acid by-products add. No empirical zinc series.

evidence.note: Sensitivity ~Rs725-750 cr per US$100/t zinc; zinc COP US$703/t (-29% y/y), FY27 guide cut to US$825-850/t
Refined metal 264 kt (+7%), mined metal 271 kt (+5%)

exposures.mechanism: Revenue is LME-USD-linked (Rs60,000 cr annualised); costs ~39% of revenue mostly INR (power, labour, contractors; some USD consumables). +3% = +Rs1,800 cr on revenue = +4.9% EBITDA; partial hedging, persistence 0.5, EV/MCap 1.0 => +2.4; trimmed to 2.2 for imported-input leakage. Rupee has strengthened 1.9% in the last month (95.8 -> 94.5), a mild headwind now.

evidence.note: Record EBITDA Rs9,285 cr at 62% margin; favourable currency movement cited in Q2

exposures.mechanism: Captive thermal power (~474 MW, model knowledge) plus coal for smelting/roasting; coal+power ~25% of cost of production but renewable round-the-clock supply is replacing coal power. Assume ~Rs3,000 cr/yr coal; +10% = Rs300 cr = -0.8% EBITDA, x0.5 persistence => -0.4. Coal e-auction premia ~94% in Sep-Oct 2026 make the shock live.

evidence.note: Cost of production guidance cut despite input pressures

exposures.mechanism: Smelters are power-intensive (Chanderiya/Debari, Dariba) but mostly self-supplied or on fixed-price renewable PPAs; assume ~15% market-exposed. +15% spot power on ~Rs800 cr = Rs120 cr = -0.3% EBITDA, x0.5 persistence => -0.2; widened for grid-curtailment tail in El Nino summer 2027.
P/E 11.6, dividend yield 2.0%, ROE 77%: a short-duration, high-payout cash cow; +25 bp on cost of equity => ~-0.8. Net-cash-ish balance sheet so direct funding effect nil.

evidence.note: P/E 11.6, mcap Rs2,41,139 cr, dividend yield 1.97%

exposures.mechanism: Royalty is paid on zinc and silver metal content; HZL's cost of production quoted excl. royalty. Assume '+1' = +2 pp rate on ~Rs6,000 cr royalty-base-equivalent => ~Rs600 cr = -1.6% EBITDA; structural (persistence 1.0), EV/MCap 1.0 => -1.6. Government of India holds 27.9% and has a fiscal interest in higher mineral levies.

Tail policy risk: a windfall levy on record silver/zinc earnings (precedent: 2022 oil export levy; event catalogue shows levies are an active tool, e.g. diesel/ATF Oct 2026). Conditional on imposition of, say, 10% of excess EBITDA => -10% EBITDA x persistence 0.4 => -4. Probability low (<10% in 12m, judgement); the edge is the conditional impact.

evidence.note: Windfall/export levy re-set on fuels (31 Oct)

exposures.mechanism: Silver (PV pastes), zinc (galvanising, grid/renewable towers, zinc-ion storage) and the Chanderiya silver refinery expansion are structural beneficiaries; +1 treated as ~+1% structural demand for silver/zinc => +0.8 via multiple. Overlaps with price edges - kept small.

evidence.note: Analyst view: demand tailwinds vs headwinds ahead for HZL

exposures.mechanism: Indian silver realisation tracks LME x USD/INR x (1+import duty); +5 pp duty (SSU defined for gold; assumed to be mirrored for silver) lifts domestic silver price ~4.5%; silver 27% of revenue => +1.2% revenue = +2% EBITDA, persistence 0.5, haircut for uncertain pass-through => +1. Rupee-silver also sits at a premium in a record-low-silver-price year.

company_links.mechanism: Parent (Vedanta Ltd, ~61% of HZL) and Vedanta Resources depend on HZL dividends to service debt; promoter holding has fallen 4.2 pp in 3 years and 54.72% of VEDL / 56.38% of VAML promoter shares are encumbered with GLAS Agency as security trustee for US$1-2.25bn financings. Parent-level stress (refinancing, further HZL block sales) hits HZL; w = % move in HZL per 1% move in VEDL. Raw weekly regression of HZL on VEDL since 2021: beta 0.36 (corr 0.44), shrunk for market component.
